Hence, the failure is classified as a network_failure with a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Current DNS timeout mirrors INC-1003; pattern suggests a recurring network/DNS issue affecting database-primary.

output.justification: The incident affects 800 users on a Tier-1 service, exceeding the 500‑user threshold defined for SEV-2. remediation_steps.title: Validate Operator Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the engineer has the required ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us‑east‑1.
verification: AWS identity ARN matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context equals prod-us-east-1

remediation_steps.title: Confirm DNS Resolution and Route53 Health Checks
remediation_steps.description: Validate that the DNS name used by database‑primary resolves correctly and that Route53 health checks are passing.
verification: DNS query returns an IP address reachable from the VPC
Health check status is 'Healthy'

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary (Failover)
remediation_steps.description: Because the primary DB is experiencing DNS‑related connectivity loss, promote the healthy read‑replica to become the new primary to restore service continuity.
verification: Replica reports status 'available' and 'Primary' role
Application connection strings point to the new primary endpoint

remediation_steps.title: Update Route53 Record Set (if needed)
remediation_steps.description: If the DNS record still points to the old primary endpoint, update the A/AAAA record to the newly promoted primary's endpoint.
verification: DNS query now returns the new primary endpoint IP
TTL reflects the updated value (60 seconds)

remediation_steps.title: Restart Dependent Services (Redis Cluster & Application Pods)
remediation_steps.description: Force a rolling restart of pods that depend on the database primary to pick up the new DNS resolution and connection endpoint.
verification: All Redis pods report READY=1/1 and STATUS=Running
All backend pods report READY=1/1 and STATUS=Running
Application logs show successful DB connections

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks and verify that error rates have returned to baseline.
commands: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/Route53 --metric-name HealthCheckStatus --dimensions Name=HealthCheckId,Value=<health‑check-id> --statistics Average --period 60 --start-time $(date -u -d '-5 minutes' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
verification: Database health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with status OK
Redis health endpoint returns HTTP 200
Route53 health check metric shows 1 (healthy) for the last 5 minutes

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert DNS record to the original primary endpoint, demote the promoted replica, and roll back any pod restarts to the pre‑remediation image tags.

steps.title: Restore Original Route53 Record
steps.description: Re‑UPSERT the DNS record to point back to the original primary endpoint.
verification: DNS query resolves to the original primary IP
TTL reflects the restored value

steps.title: Demote Replica Back to Read‑Only
steps.description: If the original primary is still functional, demote the promoted replica to read‑only mode.
verification: Replica reports status 'available' and role 'Reader'

steps.title: Rollback Deployment Images (if pods were updated)
steps.description: Undo any rollout changes to deployment images to the previous tag.
verification: Pods report the previous image tag in their container spec
No new pods are pending

steps.title: Validate System Health After Rollback
steps.description: Run the same health‑check suite used post‑remediation to ensure the environment is stable.
commands: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/Route53 --metric-name HealthCheckStatus --dimensions Name=HealthCheckId,Value=<health‑check-id> --statistics Average --period 60 --start-time $(date -u -d '-5 minutes' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
verification: All health endpoints return HTTP 200
Route53 health check metric remains healthy

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified for ProdOperations role
Current backup snapshots of database-primary and redis-cluster verified
Rollback procedures documented and approved by change management
safety_verification.notes: All steps are reversible, include verification checkpoints, and respect the write‑freeze policy before any node or service restart.
